conventions.convention: Fix the bundle, atlas and transitions z_j=g_ij⁻¹z_i. Normalized representatives satisfy a_j=a_i+λ(g_ij), with λ(h)=−ih⁻¹dh. Pushforward of horizontal distributions sends a_i to a_i−λ(h).

The Maxwell block has fixed oriented Lorentzian metric of signature (−,+,+,+), global smooth real one-form variations, and separately imposed equations d⋆dα=d⋆dβ=0. It is not the full coupled Einstein–Maxwell current.
The current ordering is ω(α,β)=α∧⋆dβ−β∧⋆dα. Its integral on a spacelike hypersurface is defined only when its coefficient relative to the induced oriented volume form is absolutely integrable.

The boundary identity treats a globally defined smooth real gauge parameter χ. Noncompact boundary-flux formulas additionally require the stated compact Borel exhaustion and finite-chain integration representatives.

Principal holonomy is the horizontal-lift fibre multiplier e^(−2πiθ); the stated Wilson variable uses the inverse convention e^(2πiθ). Gauge triviality allows smooth circle-valued gauge maps, including integer winding.
Coisotropic reduction is restricted to finite-dimensional real symplectic vector spaces, with W^ω⊆W; the zero quotient is allowed.

Countable choice is an explicit inherited background assumption for principal-connection geometry. κ₀ is a chosen positive normalization in webers; length-coordinate normalized potential components have units m⁻¹.

load_bearing.statement: Under the stated countable-choice, smooth fixed-bundle, fixed-atlas and normalization hypotheses, compatible connection representatives differ by a unique global smooth real one-form α, their normalized curvatures satisfy f′−f=dα, and their physical curvature integrals agree on every compact oriented embedded surface without boundary. The representatives form an affine space over Ω¹(M); pushforward gauge action changes a_i by −λ(h).

For global smooth normalized connection variations satisfying d⋆dα=d⋆dβ=0 on the fixed oriented Lorentzian background, define ω_g(α,β)=α∧⋆_g dβ−β∧⋆_g dα. Define Ω_Σ precisely when the pulled-back current coefficient is in L¹ of the induced positive density measure.

The stated Maxwell equations imply dω_g=0. Replacing α by α+dχ changes the current by d(χ⋆_g dβ), hence changes its finite-chain integral by the boundary integral. Under the stated absolute-integrability and exhaustion-representation hypotheses, the noncompact pairing shift equals the exhaustion-independent limiting boundary flux.
